description: Explains why Droschinsky’s edge-label reward applies only to two direct paths, while longer path pairs incur skipped-vertex penalties; compares feasible witnesses and proves penalty monotonicity in the Lean specification.

related_resources.reason: Pinned 2018 arXiv v1 / MFCS 2018, Definition 4, exact path scoring and the lead-in to Lemma 5.

learning_objectives: Compute scores for direct/direct, direct/long and long/long path pairs with signed node and edge weights
Show how changing the finite penalty changes which feasible witness scores highest
Explain forbidden weights, infinite penalty, zero penalty and negative nonempty optima
Read pathScore, one_two_path_score and maximum_score_antitone in the Lean source
